findings.title: Huge limit_window_seconds in the vendor response crashes the app on Int(Double) conversion
findings.source: Response body of GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, field rate_limit.primary_window/secondary_window.limit_window_seconds, decoded at OpenAIWireTypes.swift:76 by flexibleDoubleIfPresent
findings.sink: OpenAIWireTypes.swift:211 (and :213 for the hours branch): Int(days.rounded())
findings.description: limit_window_seconds is decoded into a Double with no range check. humanLabel only checks s > 0. A finite but huge JSON number like 1e300 passes both, days becomes about 1e295, and Int(_:) on an out-of-range Double traps. The process aborts inside decodeSnapshot.
findings.exploit_scenario: The vendor endpoint, or anything that controls the response, returns {"rate_limit":{"primary_window":{"used_percent":1,"limit_window_seconds":1e300}}}. On every refresh, OpenAIProvider.decodeSnapshot calls toSnapshot, then window(), then kind.label(from:), and the menu-bar app crashes. CachedFetch decodes before it writes the cache (CachedFetch.swift:34-36), so the bad payload is not saved and the crash does not survive a relaunch by itself. It repeats as long as the server keeps sending the value.
preconditions: attacker controls the chatgpt.com usage response (hostile or compromised vendor); TLS rules out a network MITM
findings.impact: The local monitor app is knocked out (crashes) for as long as the payload is served. No data exposure.
findings.fix: Reject non-finite or absurd values before converting, e.g. guard let s = seconds, s.isFinite, s > 0, s < 10 * 365 * 86_400 else { return default }. Or use Int(exactly:) / a clamped conversion so no trap is possible.
findings.evidence: OpenAIWireTypes.swift:207 `guard let s = seconds, s > 0` (no upper bound or isFinite check), :211/:213 `Int(days.rounded())` / `Int(hours.rounded())`. SharedCoders.decoder sets no nonConformingFloatDecodingStrategy, so only finite values arrive, but 1e300 is finite and is well past Int.max days.
